title: Semiconductor Processing
author: Dayone Koo
_comment: PROGRAM EVALUATION (evaluate-program skill), not a role report. Subject is the PROGRAM (Foothill College x TOP 094500), not a job title. Destination CANDIDATES are DERIVED: crosswalk(094500) = 21 SOCs, intersected with SECTORS['adm'].socs and minus ALL_OTHER/PROMOTION/EXPERIENCE_5YR guards = 10 (17-3013, 17-3023, 17-3024, 17-3026, 17-3027, 17-3028, 49-9012, 49-9041, 49-9043, 49-9044). Dropped by the guards: 11-3013 Facilities Managers, 17-3029 Engineering Technologists All Other, 27-1021 Commercial and Industrial Designers, 37-1011 and 47-1011 First-Line Supervisors, 47-4021 Elevator Installers, 49-9045 Refractory Materials Repairers, 49-9069 Precision Instrument Repairers All Other, 49-9071 Maintenance and Repair Workers General, 49-9081 Wind Turbine Service Technicians, 99-9999. TOP 094500 (Industrial Systems Technology and Maintenance) is a broad TOP whose crosswalk fans out across ten technician and maintenance occupations; eleven occupation columns made the 2026-09-17 draft unreadable, so `socs` is an EDITORIAL SELECTION from the candidates — 17-3026 and 17-3024, the two the crosswalk reaches that the certificate's outlines evidence (the same two the SVAMP consortium report reads this certificate against) — plus one AUTHORED ADDITION, 51-9141 Semiconductor Processing Technicians, the certificate's stated purpose (moving wafers through semiconductor processing stages in a cleanroom), which the crosswalk does not reach. Enrichments (program name, live postings, curated competencies) not yet run. EDITION 2026-09-18: crosswalk_chain true — the TOP–CIP–SOC Crosswalk section now argues the destinations; the demand note keeps only the COE sentence. DEMAND VINTAGE 2025–2030: demand figures re-read against the Centers of Excellence 2025–2030 release (2026-09-18 refresh).
lede: This evaluation assembles labor-market supply and demand evidence for Foothill College's Semiconductor Processing program (TOP 094500): regional demand for the occupations it leads to, its award and enrollment trends alongside other colleges offering the same program in the region, and how its courses align with the work of those occupations.
demand_note: [According to the Centers of Excellence](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/c01114ab-6bc3-4529-bace-e933fe293b86/page/1v72D), Semiconductor Processing Technicians (SOC 51-9141), Industrial Engineering Technologists and Technicians (SOC 17-3026) and Electro-Mechanical and Mechatronics Technologists and Technicians (SOC 17-3024) together have roughly 610 openings a year in the Bay Area.
alignment_note: The colleges offering TOP 094500 in the Bay Area, and the occupations each supports through the TOP–CIP–SOC crosswalk.
award_note: Awards conferred each year by each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.
enrollment_note: Enrollment each term in each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.
curriculum_note: O*NET maintains a set of detailed work activities that identify the competencies central to each job. Below, the Semiconductor Processing program's courses are mapped to the work activities of three of its destination occupations, based on how each course is described in its Course Outline of Record (COR).
chain_note: TOP 0945.00 spreads across four federal codes, which reach two technician occupations. Semiconductor Processing Technicians, the program's stated purpose, is not among them.
